parts.title: Leaf Day
parts.text: It was a **brisk** autumn morning. Sasha, Ollie, and Mina put on warm coats. The old maple tree was almost **bare**. Its **golden** leaves lay all over the grass.

parts.title: The Big Pile
parts.text: Sasha used a **rake** to pull the leaves into a pile. Some leaves were brown and **withered**. Ollie walked in his boots and began to **shuffle** his feet. The dry leaves went **crinkle** under each step.

parts.title: Busy Visitors
parts.text: A squirrel ran by with a **bushy** tail. It wanted to **hoard** acorns for winter. Mina set a **pumpkin** on the porch. As evening came, the light began to **fade**. Sasha and Ollie used a broom to **sweep** the porch.

parts.title: A Cozy End
parts.text: The yard was neat again. The friends jumped into the pile one last time. They laughed until it was time for hot cocoa.

definitions.meaning1: To save up and keep a lot of something. Example: Squirrels hoard nuts for winter.
definitions.meaning2: A big pile of saved things. Example: The pirate story had a hoard of coins.

definitions.meaning2: To pull things together with that tool. Example: We rake leaves into a pile.

definitions.meaning1: Shiny yellow, like gold. Example: The golden sun set behind the hills.

definitions.meaning1: To make a crackly sound or small folds. Example: The paper will crinkle when I squeeze it.
definitions.meaning2: A small fold or wrinkle. Example: There is a crinkle in my paper.

definitions.meaning1: Dried up and weak, like a plant with no water. Example: The withered flowers drooped in the vase.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ plant needed a drink of water.

definitions.meaning1: A big, round, orange fruit that grows on a vine. Example: We made soup from a pumpkin.
definitions.studentChallenge: We carved a face on a big orange ___.

definitions.meaning1: Empty, with nothing on it. Example: The tree was bare in winter.

definitions.meaning1: Cool and fresh, or quick and lively. Example: We took a brisk walk on a chilly day.
definitions.studentChallenge: A ___ wind made me pull up my hood.

definitions.meaning1: To slide your feet without lifting them. Example: I shuffle my feet in my big slippers.
definitions.meaning2: To mix up cards. Example: Please shuffle the cards before we play.
definitions.studentChallenge: He began to ___ across the room in his big socks.

definitions.meaning1: Thick and full. Example: The fox has a bushy tail.
definitions.studentChallenge: The squirrel’s ___ tail swished back and forth.

definitions.meaning1: To lose color or get dim slowly. Example: The light will fade as night comes.
definitions.studentChallenge: My red shirt began to ___ after many washes.

definitions.meaning1: To clean with a broom. Example: I sweep the kitchen floor.
definitions.meaning2: To move across quickly. Example: The wind can sweep across the field.
definitions.studentChallenge: Please ___ the dust off the porch with a broom.
